title: Only 7% Pass This Oxford Entrance Exam
summary: Arguments, assumptions and precise deductions test whether your reasoning can survive every hidden trap.

landing.intro: Arguments, patterns and logic traps collide. Can you defend the right answer when every option looks plausible?

about.body:
This worldwide entertainment challenge contains ten Oxford-inspired reasoning questions across verbal, quantitative, critical, formal, spatial and evidence-based thinking. It moves from accessible foundations to compact multi-step problems.

Choose the answer best supported by the information shown. No specialist university knowledge is required, and correctness remains hidden until the final reveal.

This is not an official Oxford University admissions test, application assessment or prediction of admission.

howToPlay.title: How to Play
steps: Complete ten carefully selected questions in one focused challenge.
Choose one answer each time. Correctness remains hidden until the final reveal.
Reveal your result, skill breakdown and complete answer review after the final question.

about.disclaimer: Independent entertainment challenge. Not an official Oxford admissions test and not affiliated with any university.

stage-1.preAdCopy: Your Oxford entrance score and three-area breakdown are ready to reveal.

profile-1.title: The Tutorial Standout
profile-1.copy: You followed difficult arguments with exceptional precision and rarely claimed more than the evidence allowed.

profile-2.title: The Oxford Natural
profile-2.copy: You crossed the challenge line with disciplined reasoning across language, logic and evidence.

profile-3.title: The Shortlisted Thinker
profile-3.copy: You handled a demanding mix of inference and analysis, with only a few traps resisting you.

profile-4.title: The Careful Reasoner
profile-4.copy: You uncovered many of the deeper rules and built a strong base for a sharper second attempt.

profile-5.title: The Promising Applicant
profile-5.copy: Several reasoning styles clicked, while the review shows where one extra check would help.

profile-6.title: The Curious Challenger
profile-6.copy: This attempt exposed some convincing traps, but every missed clue offers a useful route back in.

score.passed: You passed the Oxford entrance challenge!

oxford-s1q1.question: ARCHIVE is to RECORDS as ANTHOLOGY is to…

oxford-s1q6.question: A book costs £24 after a 20% reduction. What was its original price?

oxford-s2q2.question: A survey records 70 tutorial users and 50 library users among 100 students. Both or neither were allowed. What is the exact overlap?

oxford-s2q4.question: If an argument says a longer library day will increase attendance, which assumption does it need?
answers: Some students who cannot attend now would use the added hours

oxford-s3q3.question: Exactly one statement is true. A says ‘B is true.’ B says ‘A and C are false.’ C says ‘B is false.’ Who is true?

oxford-s3q7.question: A marker starts in the top-left corner of a square. After a 180° rotation, where does it finish?

oxford-s4q3.question: Which question exposes missing information in ‘Most students prefer tutorials’?
answers: How many students were asked and how were they selected?

oxford-s4q4.question: A candidate must submit a form and a reference. Mei submitted a form only. What follows?
answers: Mei has not yet met the stated requirement

oxford-s5q6.question: A library adds evening hours and visits rise. Which comparison best separates the hours effect from a seasonal rise?
answers: Compare with a similar library that kept its hours during the same period
Ask visitors if they like evenings

oxford-s5q7.question: A rule admits applicants with Logic ≥ 80 and Writing ≥ 70. Ava scores 84/68; Bo scores 79/90; Cy scores 82/74. Who qualifies?
